_purpose: P-205 / OPS-24 coverage-refusal lane. scripts/surface-probe.mjs could not be located in any accessible repo (legacy-design-tools, hauska-engine, hauska-map, hauska-factory, hauska-atom-contract) — see close leave_behind. This artifact substitutes hand-run live find_parcel calls through the authenticated Smart Site MCP connector (mcp__claude_ai_Smart_Site__find_parcel), same production surface a customer hits, run 2026-09-14.

reads.label: unonboarded-county-miss (the finding's own example)
reads.note: Reproduces the dispatch's cited defect live: Bell County, absent from the six-county serving ledger, returns the same 'no-hit' an in-coverage genuine miss gets. Bug confirmed still live at read time.

reads.label: unonboarded-serving-county but geocoding-populated (falsifier probe for a txgio_parcel-derived coverage check)
reads.note: DECISIVE: Bexar (48029) is NOT one of the six serving-ledger counties (48021/48055/48209/48309/48453/48491) yet find_parcel returns a REAL parcel-situs hit. This proves txgio_parcel/txgio_address (the table find_parcel's query mode actually searches) holds address data for at least one county broader than the Factory serving ledger. A coverage check derived from txgio_parcel/txgio_address row-presence would therefore classify Bexar as 'covered', which is false against the mission's own definition (an address in a county absent from the serving ledger must get the coverage refusal) — ruling out txgio-store-derived coverage as a correct source.

reads.label: onboarded-county genuine no-match (must stay no-hit, not become a false coverage refusal)
reads.expectedCounty: Bastrop (48021, one of the six serving-ledger counties)
reads.note: Baseline that must never regress: a genuine miss inside an onboarded county still returns plain no-hit today. Any future fix that widens coverage refusal must re-run this exact query and keep this result.

reads.label: regression note (fixture drift, not a finding)
reads.note: This is the exact address txgioAddressResolveCoverage.test.ts's mocked 'genuine in-coverage no-match' fixture uses. Live today it now resolves via address-point-containment (P-175, shipped after that test was written), so the test's mock is a synthetic double and does not itself prove today's live no-match behavior — the Zzyzx Trail read above is the live substitute. Not a P-205 defect; noted for whoever owns that test file.
